## Natural history notes

A small tortricid moth characterized by tan to brown forewings with darker parallel bands, fine mottling, and a folded leafroller-like resting posture. In Florida, the Parallel-banded Leafroller Moth is found in wooded and semi-wooded habitats such as hammocks, forest edges, pine flatwoods, parks, yards, and shrubby areas where suitable host plants occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed concealed in rolled or tied leaves, using silk shelters for protection and serving as prey for birds, bats, spiders, and parasitoid wasps.
